source.title: Deep Learning on a Data Diet: Finding Important Examples Early in Training
source.authors: Mansheej Paul; S. Ganguli; G. Dziugaite

record.tranche_reason: The study tests how a small amount of randomized label noise affects test accuracy under EL2N-based data selection, but it does not test fitting fully random labels.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a clean-label and 10%-randomized-label sliding-window pruning experiment. It does not report whether the networks fit the randomized training labels, nor does it sweep noise from none to all. The cited random-label protocol from Zhang et al. is prior work, not this study's result.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates data pruning and noise identification using clean labels and 10% label corruption. It does not measure random-label training fit, convergence costs, degradation across corruption levels, or the temporal ordering of learning signal and memorizing noise. Reusing Zhang et al.'s corruption protocol does not itself test a claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record correctly identifies the noise-related pruning conclusion, but 'shifts upward' is unsupported: the authors say the optimal window shifts to exclude more highest-scoring examples. They also report higher early EL2N scores for corrupted labels and reduced kernel velocity at the highest scores. They do not establish whether networks ultimately fit the corrupted labels.
record.recipe_differences: The experiment randomizes 10% of labels and evaluates final test accuracy after training on selected subsets; it does not train on wholly random labels or measure their training fit.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported pruning-window outcome differs between clean labels and 10% randomized labels.

fits_no_version.finding: With 10% corrupted labels, optimal EL2N windows exclude more of the highest-scoring examples; Figures 2 and 16 report final accuracy after subset selection.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Label corruption increases the benefit of excluding very high EL2N examples when selecting training subsets.

fits_no_version.finding: At the early scoring checkpoint, corrupted-label examples tend to have higher EL2N scores than clean-label examples, and corruption increases their scores (Appendix F.2, Figure 17). This does not track subsequent memorization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early prediction-error norms can help distinguish corrupted-label examples from clean-label examples.

fits_no_version.finding: With label noise, NTK velocity drops sharply for the highest EL2N examples (Section 5.1, Figure 3). The suggestion that learning gives up on these examples is a hypothesis, without a measurement of their eventual training fit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Label noise changes the relationship between example difficulty and feature-kernel evolution.

record.problems: For the label-noise result, only clean labels and 10% randomized labels are compared; the excerpted figure provides no exact values, and the text does not report training error or unpruned test accuracy across noise levels.
record.rows_left_out: The Fig. 2 and Fig. 16 sliding-window plots show final test accuracy by offset for clean and 10%-randomized labels, but the reported outcome concerns data pruning and does not establish the training-fit or smooth noise-degradation behavior specified by V4. No rows meet the claim-version row criteria.

untested.parts: Training fit and chance-level test performance with completely random labels under unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative time to fit true and random labels, and convergence speed across corruption fractions.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit while test error increases steadily toward chance across a corruption sweep. Pruned-subset accuracy at 0% and 10% corruption does not establish this behavior.
Whether explicit regularizers prevent random-label fitting, and whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
Whether networks learn shared real-data patterns before subsequently memorizing noise. Early EL2N distributions and kernel velocities do not establish this temporal sequence.

record.verdict_notes: Replace the record's tests/T2 classification and V4 tested status. There are no extracted rows to fix and no omitted results directly testing a claim version.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment measures training error or test error when all training labels are randomly assigned.
No comparison of training time or convergence speed across label-noise fractions.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiment.

The paper tests clean labels versus 10% randomized labels in a pruning-window experiment, but does not report training-set fit, a smooth sweep toward 100% corruption, or test error for an unpruned model across corruption levels.
No comparison tests whether regularizers prevent fitting random labels or whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
No training-dynamics comparison of when real-label patterns and noisy or random labels are learned.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
